text.p: Italian debt markets collapsed in an exhausted heap after seven successive days of gains and record highs, with profit-taking setting in late European trade.

The eighth day of rallying just proved too much and the September Btp futures contract on LIFFE stood 28 basis points down at 132.80 after first galloping up to a record high at 133.70 and then swinging to the day's low of 132.55.
Traders said the aim was 134.00 but difficulty in taking out a barrier at 133.70 meant players started taking profits.
The February 2007 Btp slithered 40 basis points to end at 98.80 with the spread over Bunds back at 126 basis points.
The Btp-Bund spread had wound into a record 121 basis points on convergence optimism earlier.
"The market needs to calm down a bit," one broker at a London-based brokerage said. "We started at 129, this was the eighth session of rallying and we're on the upper side of the channel," he added.

Strength started to fade in the afternoon session and then comments from new French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin helped spark further profit-taking when Jospin said he was committed to launching the euro on time but significantly failed to mention meeting tough Maastricht criteria.

At home, dealers noted talks on reforming spending in the Italian welfare sector had got off to a less than brilliant start with the hard-left and trade unions both saying the government's position had to change.

However the first focus is preliminary inflation data from 11 sample Italian cities, with five cities releasing their data on Friday and the rest on Monday. Analysts are forecasting a year on year rate of 1.5 to 1.6 percent, but dealers say prospects for an interest rate cut have really receded into the middle distance for now.
